question.text: Kaveri Credit Opps funds INR 100 crore of mezzanine debt at a 12% cash coupon (paid annually at year-end) + 3% PIK + 2% equity warrants (strike at current round). 3-year bullet repayment. At exit at the end of year 3, the equity warrants convert and are sold for INR 25 crore additional proceeds. Approximate gross IRR (ignoring fees)?

answer.text: Approximately 21-22% — cash coupon, PIK compounding and the warrant equity uplift together.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines IRR / yield on the basis of cash-flow timing and describes equity kickers within mezzanine / private-credit structures. With annual coupons of 12 crore at the end of years 1-3, PIK at 3% compounding to about 9.27 crore added to the year-3 inflow, principal of 100 crore repaid at year 3, and warrant proceeds of 25 crore at year 3, the resulting IRR works out to approximately 21-22% over the three-year period. The Trap: Options A and B ignore the equity-kicker contribution. Option D overshoots the cash-flow profile. Note: IRR / yield cash-flow timing is covered on pages 143 and 149-150, and equity kickers within mezzanine / private credit appear on page 211. The workbook quotes a venture-debt IRR range on page 213 but does not state a separate mezzanine-IRR band.
